source.snippet: I've got a bunch of Mailman3 mailing lists, but one of them has 500+ users, and about 60 of them are on @rochester.rr.com. RoadRunner has been bouncing all or nearly all the emails because of either too many recipients per connection, or too many simultaneous connections. [Sysadmin managing community/org mailing lists, spending time configuring Postfix throttling manually]

problem_statement: Operators running self-hosted mailing lists (Mailman3/Postfix) waste significant configuration time manually tuning per-domain outbound connection throttling to satisfy ISP rate limits, and still suffer delivery failures when ISP policies change silently.
target_segment: Sysadmins and DevOps engineers managing self-hosted bulk mailing lists for organizations, communities, or SaaS products
notes: Single signal but professional/ops context is clear. The pain is recurring (ISP rate limits change, requiring ongoing tuning). A managed deliverability layer or a Postfix config-as-a-service for self-hosters could charge monthly. Weaker signal than the Salesforce cluster — only one data point here.
